Test if a target variable equals a specified value or another variable's value

Source: R/ac_tags.R
ac_test.Rd

This function is designed to test ac-tags by comparing values in a dataframe. It takes a dataframe as input and tests whether the variable given by target_var equals either a fixed value or the values of another variable in the dataframe (target_value). Optionally, a conditional subset of the data can be specified to restrict the test.

The function reports success if all tested rows meet the condition. If any rows do not meet the condition, it prints case IDs and relevant variables (including those specified in print_filter_vars) for debugging, then stops with an error.

Usage

ac_test(
  data,
  target_var,
  target_value,
  condition_var = NULL,
  operator = "equal",
  condition_value = NULL,
  print_filter_vars = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A dataframe (typically a neps field-data dataframe).

target_var

A string specifying the name of the variable to test in the dataframe.

target_value

Either:

  • a numeric vector of expected values, or

  • a string specifying the name of another variable in the dataframe whose values are compared against target_var.

condition_var

Optional string specifying a variable name to subset/filter the data before testing.

operator

Optional string specifying the comparison operator used for subsetting. One of: "equal", "unequal", "greater", "smaller", "greaterequal", "smallerequal", or "inlist". Defaults to "equal".

condition_value

Optional numeric or character value used in conjunction with condition_var and operator to subset the data before testing.

print_filter_vars

Optional character vector specifying additional variable names whose columns should be prioritized and displayed early in error prints to assist debugging (e.g. variables used in filter() prior to calling ac_test).

Value

Invisibly returns NULL. Function either prints a success message or stops with a detailed error.

Details

The function expects caseid column in the data by default and always includes it in output. When errors occur, output tables prioritize columns in the following order: caseid, target_var, variables in print_filter_vars, then all other columns.

See also

Other test functions: date_test_complex(), ef_test(), label_test(), value_label_test()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Simple test that h_etumf equals 1
ac_test(mydata, target_var = "h_etumf", target_value = 1)

# Test that h_etumf equals values of another variable h_expected
ac_test(mydata, target_var = "h_etumf", target_value = "h_expected")

# Test on a subset of data where etazv is between 15 and 90, prioritizing etazv in error prints
filtered_data <- mydata %>% filter(etazv %in% c(15:90, -20))
ac_test(filtered_data, target_var = "h_etumf", target_value = 1,
        print_filter_vars = c("etazv"))
} # }
